_comment: THE DECLARATION FILE FOR NUMBERED BROWSER SUITES.
There is ONE list of what the release gate runs: BROWSER_SUITES in
scripts/run-platform-tests.sh. This file is not a second copy of it. It is
the place a suite that deliberately does NOT run in that gate is declared,
with the reason, so that 'it is not in the runner' is always either a
recorded decision or a failure -- never an oversight nobody can see.
scripts/verify-browser-suite-registry.mjs enforces it: every numbered file
in scripts/browser-verification/ must be in BROWSER_SUITES or listed here.
Adding a suite and forgetting the runner now fails the gate on the commit
that adds it, which is the only moment anyone still remembers why.
Convergence Step 7 found twenty-seven fixture-operations suites outside the
runner and twelve of them broken. This file exists so that cannot recur
silently. A reason here is a commitment, not a dismissal.

exempt.45-capability-foundation: SUPERSEDED by the SQL estate, which runs in the canonical gate and asserts the same foundation far more thoroughly: capability_precedence_truth_table.sql (50 assertions over the full rule 0-8 order), capability_scope_isolation.sql (22) and step8_operational_access.sql (69). Measured at Step 8: this suite aborts after 4 assertions waiting for a club allow that the current screen no longer renders the way it expects. The authority it guarded is guarded; the browser journey it walked no longer exists.
exempt.46-family-authority: FAMILY DOMAIN, NOT YET RECONCILED -- but no longer an isolation problem. BATCH A REPAIRED ITS TEARDOWN. The reason recorded here before was that its identities could not be removed at all, because public.audit_log is append-only under internal.refuse_history_rewrite(). That was not what was actually blocking it. The cleanup owned players by TAGGED SURNAME only, so a player the PRODUCT named -- an approved Add Child creates one carrying no tag -- held a place in the run's own team, and the teams delete was refused by player_team_memberships_team_id_fkey; the suite died in setup before asserting anything. Batch A redrew the ownership boundary where the relationships actually are: a place in a team THIS RUN created is this run's to remove, a player one of this run's throwaway identities CREATED is this run's player, and a guardian link is owned from BOTH ends. A player holding any team place outside the run's own club is left alone. Measured after the repair: two consecutive runs, identical results, three passed and two failed, ZERO cleanup errors and ZERO residue -- no slice4a users, clubs, teams or players remain. It is now independently repeatable. IT STAYS EXEMPT because A2 and A4 still fail: the Add Child flow completes in the browser and shows 'Waiting for Your Club', yet writes neither a players row nor a player_duplicate_reviews row. That is the Add Child inconsistency Step 9 already DEFERRED to family-domain reconciliation, and Batch A did not change product architecture to make another domain's suite green. OWNER: the family domain. A suite with failing assertions is never gate coverage.

exempt.91-mobile-foundation: THE MOBILE APP'S OWN ACCEPTANCE JOURNEY, and it is declared here rather than wired into the release runner because it needs a server the release runner does not start: the Expo dev server on :8081. Adding `expo start` to the web gate would make every web release wait on a React Native bundler, which is a cost paid by the wrong programme. It is not unverified -- it passes 27 of 27 and has been run twice with zero residue, seeding and removing its own disposable identity each time. RUN IT WITH: `cd apps/mobile && npx expo start --web --port 8081` then `node scripts/browser-verification/91-mobile-foundation.mjs`. It runs against Expo Web because this machine has no iOS simulator (Xcode is not installed) and no Android SDK; that is the same component tree and the same navigation, but it does NOT exercise expo-secure-store, which has no web implementation. Mobile milestone M11 owns wiring this into a mobile release gate of its own.
exempt.92-mobile-shell: THE MOBILE SHELL'S UX PROOF -- launch continuity, the bottom bar's labels and touch targets, four viewport widths from 320 to 430, axe on every destination and on the context sheet, and losing signal while the app is running. Declared here for the same reason as 91-mobile-foundation: it needs the Expo dev server on :8081, which the web release runner does not start and should not have to. It passes 31 of 31. RUN IT WITH: `cd apps/mobile && npx expo start --web --port 8081` then `node scripts/browser-verification/92-mobile-shell.mjs`. Safe-area insets are ZERO on Expo Web, so it proves the layout does not DEPEND on them being non-zero; the notch, the Dynamic Island and the home indicator are covered by the physical-iPhone checklist in docs/mobile/DEVELOPMENT.md.
